en: CROSS! VORHALT'S SELLING A MUSEUM'S ALARM PLANS TO A GANG OF ART THIEVES. GO AND GET THEM!
_where: Mission 1's briefing, line 1 (BISHOP, the General)
_note: LB: Bishop calls Cross "du" and "Jong" (son, boy); Vesper calls the General "Dir" and "Generol" (lod.lu).

en: HE'S ALREADY GOT THEM, GENERAL. HE'S RUNNING FOR THE CHOPPER.
_where: Mission 1's briefing, line 2 (VESPER, the briefer)
_note: LB: "Déi huet en schonn": he already has them.

en: THAT'S MY BOY! AND THAT CHOPPER'S ON THE METER, SON. FUEL DOESN'T GROW ON TREES.
_where: Mission 1's briefing, line 3 (BISHOP)
_note: JOKE: "Fuel doesn't grow on trees" twists "money doesn't grow on trees". Luxembourgish has the same saying ("D'Geld wiisst net op de Beem"), so the twist carries straight over: "Sprit wiisst net op de Beem". "On the meter" (rented by the minute, like a taxi) is "de Compteur leeft".

en: IT COMES OUT OF THE COFFEE MACHINE BUDGET. WHICH IS WHY WE DON'T HAVE A COFFEE MACHINE.
_where: Mission 1's briefing, line 4 (VESPER)
_note: JOKE: The chopper's fuel comes out of the coffee-machine budget, so there is no coffee machine. Kept as it is.

en: ONE GUARD ON THE PAD. HUGE. MINIGUN. SKULL ON HIS CHEST. NAME TAG SAYS ARDBALLS.
_where: Mission 1's briefing, line 5 (VESPER)
_note: JOKE: ARDBALLS (like Odd Job; "hard balls") is a name and stays in English: the joke is the name tag. "Doudekapp" = skull (and crossbones).

_where: Mission 1's briefing, line 6 (CROSS)
_note: JOKE: Cross's cool line: keep the taxi meter running (I'll be right back). Bishop says the same words when Cross dies (M1_KILLED_02), so both must stay word for word the same.

_where: Mission 1's end conversation after an escape: the red tag top left

en: GOOD RIDDANCE, ARDBALLS! SON, ARE THE ALARM PLANS SAFE?
_where: Mission 1, after an escape, line 1 (BISHOP)
_note: JOKE: "Good riddance, ARDBALLS!" (a new ARDBALLS turns up every mission: the running gag). Lb: "Äddi, Ardballs, a komm net zeréck!" (bye, and don't come back), which sets up the next one coming back. A better Luxembourgish "good riddance" welcome.

_where: Mission 1, after an escape, line 2 (CROSS)
_note: JOKE: Pun: the ALARM plans, "no need to be alarmed". Lb: "Kee Grond fir Alarm" (no reason for alarm) keeps it, with "Alarmpläng" in the line before.

_where: Mission 1, after an escape, line 3 (VESPER)
_note: JOKE: Running gag: Vesper scores Cross's one-liner out of ten, always low.

en: FOUR? THAT'S ERNEST CROSS YOU'RE SCORING!
_where: Mission 1, after an escape, line 4 (BISHOP)
_note: JOKE: Bishop outraged: "That's ERNEST Cross you're scoring!" (Ernest sounds like "earnest"). Lb keeps the outrage ("den Ernest Cross, deen s du do bewäerts!"); the earnest pun is lost (Lb "eescht" = earnest, if you find a way in).

en: STILL A FOUR. AND WHILE WE'RE ON NUMBERS, I'D LIKE A RAISE.
_where: Mission 1, after an escape, line 5 (VESPER)
_note: JOKE: "While we're on numbers, I'd like a raise." Lb: "a wa mer schonn bei den Zuele sinn: ech hätt gär méi Pai."

en: DENIED. NOW GLIDE HOME, SON. SAVES FUEL.
_where: Mission 1, after an escape, line 6 (BISHOP)
_note: JOKE: The stingy General: "glide home, saves fuel". Lb: "Schwief heem" (schwiewen = glide, float), "dat spuert Sprit".
